summary.text: 汉 is the simplified form of 漢, whose earliest supported use here names the Han River. The traditional graph combines a water marker with a proposed sound element whose identity remains disputed.

formation.text: The traditional graph 漢 is analyzed as phonosemantic: 水 marks the water category, while its right side is proposed to supply a sound cue. The received analysis calls that side an abbreviated 難; another suggests 堇, and other accounts associate early forms with 𦰩 or 熯. 汉 is the simplified form corresponding to 漢.

components.text: 氵 is the conventional side form of 水. In 漢 it marks the water category relevant to the river name; it does not depict the river itself.

The right side of 漢 is disputed: the received analysis calls it reduced 難, another suggests 堇, and other accounts associate early forms with 𦰩 or 熯. Zhengzhang’s reconstructed readings make 熯 a possible sound comparison, but do not establish that it names the element in the early graph.

sound_limitation.text: The comparison with 熯 does not establish that 熯 identifies the right-side element in the earliest graph, and no reading for 𦰩 itself is established here.

sound.text: A proposed analysis associates this right side with 熯. In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system, one reading of 熯 is *hnaːns, matching 漢 *hnaːns; 熯 also has the reading *hnaːnʔ. This sound comparison does not prove that 熯 names the early graph’s element.

components.text: 又 is the visible right-side element in simplified 汉, corresponding graphically to material on the right of 漢. This does not show that the traditional element meant 又 or that 又 retains a former sound role.

history.text: A modern comparison places a form attributed to the 京師畯尊 beside later traditional 漢 and simplified 汉. The inscription is read as naming the Han River; its attribution and proposed date are scholarly identifications, and the date is argued rather than established absolutely.

The traditional graph’s right side has competing analyses: abbreviated 難, proposed 堇, and associations with 𦰩 or 熯; some accounts also report confusion with 黃. These claims do not establish a single sequence of graphic changes. 汉 corresponds to 漢 as its simplified form and is also described as adapted from cursive writing, with 又 visible on the right.

uncertainties.text: The inscription’s proposed date is an epigraphist’s argument. The Han River’s original spoken name and its prehistory remain unresolved.

The traditional graph’s right element has disputed identity and pronunciation. Its precise relationship to 難, 堇, 𦰩, 熯, and 黃 remains unresolved; the reported 熯 comparison does not verify that analysis.

Examples use 漢 for both the Han River and the Milky Way, but do not show which sense came first or whether one developed from the other. The chronology of dynasty, ethnic, language, and person uses is incomplete.
The 1956 simplification scheme’s broad effective date is reported, but the individual listing for 汉 and any earlier cursive or popular antecedent are not verified here.

senses.period: Early Western Zhou attribution; absolute date argued
senses.text: The 京師畯尊 inscription is read as using 漢 for the Han River. This is the earliest supported use here, though its dating is argued rather than established absolutely.

senses.period: Book of Odes quotation; first date unresolved
senses.text: A Book of Odes quotation uses 漢 for the Milky Way. The available examples do not show that this meaning developed from the river name.

senses.gloss: Han dynasty or its political label
senses.text: 漢 is used for the Han dynasty and its political label. A naming account connects the dynasty with the Han fief and Hanzhong, which it associates with the Han River, but this does not establish a direct semantic transition or complete chronology.

senses.period: Process reported from around the sixth century CE; stabilization later
senses.text: 漢 became an ethnic or cultural label associated with the prestige of the Han dynasty. The timing and stabilization are debated, and the earliest securely dated example is unresolved.
漢 appears in terms for the Chinese language. The date and semantic route to this use are unresolved.

developments.text: The ethnic-cultural label is associated with the prestige of the Han dynasty. Its timing and stabilization are debated, and no exact first attestation is established here.

limitations.text: The river and Milky Way examples do not establish which sense came first or whether one developed from the other.
The dating or semantic route for the language sense, and the full chronology among river, dynasty, ethnic, and other recorded uses, remain unresolved.
The evidence supports a water-semantic construction for the river name and does not demonstrate that the whole graph was borrowed to write an unrelated word.

takeaway.text: The river and Milky Way meanings are not proven to derive from each other. Later uses for the dynasty, Han people, and Chinese language are not all securely dated.
